clue.text: Bearish old City function

parts.note: Ur of the Chaldees was an ancient Mesopotamian city
sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A gloomy report on the state of a traditional City of London financial function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' tempts the solver towards the London financial district, but here it is the ancient city of Ur.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursine means of or like a bear, so bearish in the literal animal sense.

clue.text: A Continental pair split up

parts.note: un is French for a
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A European couple separates.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple is to detach or separate things joined together.

clue.text: House on deferred terms, say, belonging to an Arab

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house

indicators.note: the word say indicates the following word is heard rather than spelled

parts.note: on tick means on credit

explanation.surface: A home bought on credit, owned by an Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to spell TIC, which sounds like TICK, a British informal word for credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabs are a Semitic people, speaking a language of that family.

clue.text: A casino is, in essence, a bit of a racket

indicators.note: a bit of a phrase shows the solver should take a run of letters from within the words

explanation.surface: A casino is basically a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' reads as a swindle, but means din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, so the quality of being loud.

clue.text: Raise signal to change ends

parts.note: in cricket, when the umpire calls over the fielders and bowling change ends of the pitch
a call is a signal or summons

explanation.surface: Someone lifting a flag as a cue to swap sides of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: an over is a set of six balls, after which play switches to the other end of the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, an overcall is a bid that raises above the opponent's opening bid.

clue.text: A lunar deviant — one disposed to worry about his health

annotationWithheld.why: A lunar deviant — one disposed to worry about his health (14): the anagram fodder A LUNAR DEVIANT plus I (one) gives the answer, so 'deviant' is both fodder and the only anagram indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: A lunar deviant — one disposed to worry about his health

clue.text: "O what a and peasant slave am I" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "O what a and peasant slave am I" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "O what a and peasant slave am I" (Hamlet)
parts.note: the missing word in Hamlet's soliloquy where he berates himself as a rascal

explanation.surface: Hamlet scolds himself in his soliloquy.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Hamlet, Act 2: the gap holds the word he calls himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet calls himself a rascal, a scoundrel, in the soliloquy after the players' scene.

clue.text: Prompt service needed for car indicator

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a cue is a signal or indicator

explanation.surface: Fast servicing is required for a car's flashing indicator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like 'quick', but it is a noun: a prompt to a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocue is a screen device that prompts presenters with their script.

clue.text: Young chap admits university course has folded

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lad is a young chap
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, an Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: A young man admits his university course has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folded' looks like 'failed', but means laid over itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapped means wrapped or laid over, one layer upon another.

clue.text: Written instruction detailing the business to be done

definitions.text: Written instruction detailing the business to be done

parts.words: Written instruction detailing the business to be done
parts.note: theatre 'business' is an actor's movements and actions, set out in the script

explanation.surface: A commercial memo sets out the tasks for a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business' suggests commerce, but in theatre it means an actor's incidental actions on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Playwrights write these notes in the script telling actors how to move and act.

clue.text: Order for imprisonment — or burial?

definitions.meaning: a court's warrant sending someone to prison
the moment a coffin is lowered into the grave at a funeral

explanation.definitionFit: A committal sends a person to jail, and the committal at a funeral consigns the body to the earth.

clue.text: Climb in gear

definitions.meaning: rise from bed or a chair, as a phrasal verb

explanation.definitionFit: To get up is to rise; a get-up is an outfit someone is wearing.

clue.text: Resolution for the withdrawal of bonds

definitions.meaning: the undoing or solving of a knotty problem
loosening ropes or ties that hold something

explanation.definitionFit: Unknotting a problem resolves it, and loosening fetters frees what they held.

clue.text: It supported three well-bred girls

parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of three sisters living at the bottom of a well who lived on a sticky syrup drawn from it; well-bred means raised in a well

explanation.surface: A charity that funded the upbringing of three refined young ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-bred' reads as 'refined', but the girls were literally bred in a well, in the Dormouse's tale at the Mad Tea-Party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dormouse's three sisters lived on this golden syrup, drawn from their well.

clue.text: Shakespearian heroine loses church money

indicators.note: the heroine is said to lose something, so letters are taken away from her name

parts.note: Lucrece is the heroine of Shakespeare's poem The Rape of Lucrece
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A Shakespearian heroine's church gives up its funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is an old, often scornful word for cash or profit.

clue.text: Made a penny for each bird

parts.note: did means made, as in did a job
per means for each, as in per head

explanation.surface: Someone earned a penny for every bird they handled.
explanation.definitionFit: The didapper is an old name for the dabchick, or little grebe, a diving waterbird.

clue.text: Traveller's fare

definitions.meaning: a paying customer of a taxi

explanation.definitionFit: A taxi driver's fare is the person they carry, a rider on board.

clue.text: Diamond held in the hand

parts.note: a slang word for a gem is also a hand-held firework that throws off glittering sparks

explanation.surface: Someone holds a diamond in their hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses: slang for a diamond, and a firework held in the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a gem, and a firework on a wire held while it fizzes.

clue.text: Strap left buckled on leather breastplate

indicators.note: something buckled is bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A strap on the left side is fastened over a leather breastplate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckled' looks like fastening a strap, but it signals the anagram of STRAP and L, giving PLASTR.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastron is a padded leather chest protector worn in fencing.

clue.text: Name G A Sala made up — Italian, of course

indicators.note: made up means invented, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Victorian journalist G A Sala invented a name, which is of course Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: George Augustus Sala was a Victorian journalist; 'of course' means a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagna is an Italian pasta dish served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Off the top of one's head, one might call it a trophy

definitions.text: Off the top of one's head, one might call it a trophy

parts.words: Off the top of one's head, one might call it a trophy
parts.note: the idiom for speaking spontaneously is taken literally: skin cut from the crown of an enemy's head and kept as a prize

explanation.surface: An offhand remark that a prize is a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off the top of one's head' means impromptu, but here it means literally taken from the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors once cut the skin and hair from a defeated enemy's head and kept it as a victory token.

clue.text: Changed to high note on reed, perhaps

parts.note: in alt means high in pitch; alt is a high note

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible rearrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A musician switches to a high note on a reed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Altered means made different, modified.

clue.text: Uneasy about German with forger's shop

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: shy means timid or ill at ease
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: Someone nervous about a German with a counterfeiter's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' looks like a counterfeiter, but is a blacksmith who forges metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A smithy is the workshop of a blacksmith, who forges iron.

clue.text: Boy with degree in charge of stone work

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A young man with a qualification supervises building in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonic is the adjective from mason, a builder who works with dressed stone.

clue.text: Sounding like the letter n of 'organ'

definitions.text: Sounding like the letter n of 'organ'

parts.words: Sounding like the letter n of 'organ'
parts.note: the n is pronounced through the nose, the organ of smell

explanation.surface: A speech teacher describes the final consonant of the word organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the musical instrument, but is the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: N is a consonant voiced through the nose.

clue.text: Female ruff and variegated tern come down to earth

parts.note: a reeve or ree is the female of the ruff, a wading bird

indicators.note: variegated means patchy or varied, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Two birds, a female ruff and a mottled tern, land on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variegated' turns TERN into ENTER; 'come down to earth' reads as landing birds but means a spacecraft returning through the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsule coming back from space re-enters the atmosphere to land.

clue.text: Label American flower in Spain

parts.note: a tag is a label

explanation.surface: Someone attaches a tag to an American flower growing in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows: a river. The Tagus is the longest river of Iberia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus is a river rising in Spain and reaching the sea at Lisbon.

clue.text: Opening in profit, say by a pound

parts.note: taken as written
profit sounds like prophet, and an augur is a prophet
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: Getting into profit, perhaps by a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'say' tells you that 'profit' should be heard as 'prophet', whose synonym AUGUR is then used.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural event is the first one, marking the start of something.

clue.text: Truly the right heath for a young horse

parts.note: yea is an old word meaning truly or indeed
R is the abbreviation for right
ling is heather, the plant of the heath

explanation.surface: Indeed, the heath on the right is the ideal place for a colt.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse in its second year, between one and two years old.

clue.text: He ranks as a Leveller

definitions.meaning: someone who sorts or classifies by quality
a machine that flattens a road surface

explanation.definitionFit: One who sorts by quality, and also a road-building machine that flattens ground.
